functional_lineage.updater: Fetches origin/main, computes changed files/services, saves pre-update SHA, stops affected services, fast-forward pulls, optionally pip-installs changed requirements, reloads systemd, restarts services, runs health/model checks and can git-reset to the saved SHA on selected failures.
functional_lineage.recovery: Interactive destructive DB reset path: stop services -> backup live DB directory -> unlink live DB/WAL/SHM files -> copy reference DBs/invariants from repository -> restart prior active services.
functional_lineage.entrypoints: Desktop/tray/standalone wrappers expose the same update and recovery engines; updater supports --yes auto-confirm and 6-hour tray update checks, while recovery confirmation defaults to false.
functional_lineage.packaging: PyInstaller specs explicitly set codesign_identity=None; packaging itself provides no code-signing trust anchor.

confirmed_current_at_frozen_head: model auto-repair downloads via wget and validates only a minimum byte size before replacement
service health check reports done in both all_ok branches and returns True even when services are inactive
recovery backs up then wipes/copies DB files and reports completion without an integrity/health rollback gate

safety_findings.evidence: step_start_services warns on failed starts but returns True; step_health_check sets status to done whether all_ok is true or false and always returns True. Main run invokes both without checking return values and then prints the success path.
safety_findings.effect: An update can be declared successful while one or more affected services failed to start or remain unhealthy. Rollback is not triggered by this failure class.
safety_findings.required_contract: Post-update activation and health are commit gates. Any required service failure must abort the update transaction and restore the prior verified release/state, or explicitly enter a degraded recovery state that cannot be labeled success.

safety_findings.evidence: _download_model downloads directly from configured HTTPS URLs to a temporary path and accepts/replaces the target when file size exceeds min_bytes. No expected digest/signature is bound in MODEL_REGISTRY or checked in this path.
safety_findings.effect: Artifact identity is not cryptographically established; a wrong/corrupted/compromised artifact of plausible size can become the active model/voice file.
safety_findings.required_contract: Every executable/model/data artifact must be content-addressed or signature-verified before activation. Registry entries require expected digest/signature/provenance and atomic verified install.

safety_findings.evidence: Update commits are accepted from configured origin/main via git fetch/pull --ff-only and changed requirements trigger pip install -r. The updater itself does not verify a pinned commit allowlist/signature or hashed dependency lock before activation.
safety_findings.effect: Repository/remote or dependency-channel compromise can propagate into the running agent with its local authority.
safety_findings.required_contract: Separate discovery from authorization: fetch candidate release, verify signed/content-addressed release manifest and dependency lock, stage in isolated environment, run Harness gates, then atomically activate.

safety_findings.evidence: Recovery makes a file copy backup, wipes live DB files, copies reference files, starts services, and returns success. Failed service starts are warnings; no SQLite integrity checks, schema/invariant validation, reference manifest digest, or automatic restore-from-backup path is executed before success.
safety_findings.effect: A failed or incompatible reference restore can leave the live state replaced while the tool announces completion; the backup exists but restoration from it is manual/out-of-band.
safety_findings.required_contract: Recovery must be a staged transaction: immutable snapshot -> validate reference manifest/hashes/schema -> restore into staging -> integrity/invariant checks -> boot/health probe -> atomic swap. Failure automatically restores the snapshot.

safety_findings.evidence: Recovery explicitly unlinks all current DB files after an interactive confirmation. The path is deliberately destructive, though reversible only via retained backups.
safety_findings.effect: This operation cannot belong to ordinary autonomous Frank/Needle authority under the current no-destructive-action Clay alignment target.
safety_findings.required_contract: Expose recovery as a privileged reversible maintenance transaction requiring explicit external/user authorization; ordinary model-generated action paths may inspect/prepare but cannot execute the destructive commit.

positive_controls: Updater saves the exact pre-update Git SHA and uses fast-forward-only pull.
Updater scopes service restarts to changed-file mappings and has an update lock.
Model downloads use temporary files before replacement and have timeout/min-size checks.
Recovery confirmation defaults to No and makes a timestamped backup before wiping.
Recovery stops services before DB copy operations and retains up to three backup directories.

needle: Ordinary effect authority must not include destructive DB wipe/reset or unverified software/model activation.
Model/code update is a privileged transaction, not a generic shell effect.
harness: Add fault-injection gates for failed service start, failing /health, corrupted model of valid size, bad DB schema, interrupted copy, dependency-install failure and rollback failure.
No green success state unless post-activation health and invariant gates pass.
claycode: Represent UpdateCandidate, VerifiedArtifact, StagedRelease, Activation, RollbackSnapshot and DestructiveRecoveryCommit as distinct effect types with authority levels.
A destructive commit primitive must be unavailable to normal generated ClayCode; preparation/verification can remain autonomous.
unifieddb: Snapshots and recovery should be database-native consistent checkpoints, not ad-hoc copies of live multi-file state.
Persist release/recovery manifests with hashes, schema versions and snapshot ancestry.
claygraph: Record release and recovery ancestry as immutable graph edges: previous release -> candidate -> verified -> activated or rolled_back.
frank: Frank may reason about and recommend updates/recovery, but runtime authority must distinguish cognition from privileged state mutation.
gwt: Broadcast proposed/verified/activated/failed/rolled_back update states separately so a failed health check cannot be represented as completed success.
clay: One-binary dissolution must strengthen, not erase, the transaction boundary: central artifact verification + activation gate + rollback is required before module fusion.
